newsitem.title: USA: Tandy to complete Sprint add-on by 1997 Q3.
newsitem.headline: Tandy to complete Sprint add-on by 1997 Q3.

text.p: Tandy Corp expects to have all 6,800 of its RadioShack stores fitted with a Sprint Corp "store-within-a-store" by the third quarter of 1997, company executives told reporters in a teleconference.
The transition will necessitate RadioShack pulling some products carried in its stores, but the company said Wednesday those products will be sold via catalog.

The 10-year marketing alliance linking Tandy, Sprint and Sprint Spectrum will give RadioShack customers access to Sprint Spectrum personal communications services, Sprint long distance, local and wireless service, and Internet access.
Leonard Roberts, RadioShack president, would not identify specific product category reductions but said those removed were not significant gross margin contributors.
Besides, he said, items physically withdrawn from store shelves could still be sold through the company's catalog.
RadioShack devotes eight to 10 percent of its space to telecommunications products. Under the new agreement, Sprint's store-within-a-store will occupy 15 percent of the space.
Tandy chairman John Roach, in answer to a question, said RadioShack was unlikely to be selling AT&T Corp or MCI Communications Corp products in its outlets.

Under the agreement, Roach said "for us to accomplish our mutual objectives, Sprint products and services will be very pervasive at RadioShack." He said in areas where Sprint could not offer certain products, the company has the option of marketing products made by Sprint competitors.

Roach said RadioShack will receive a gross margin of Sprint products it sells. If services are involved, it gets fees for selling that service as well as residual revenues from add-on services. In addition, he said the company will receive specific advertising support for most of the services sold.
Sprint chairman William Esrey said he expects RadioShack to be a primary retail distribution channel for the company.
"But we fully expect to market through other distribution channels -- but not within a store-within-a-store concept," he said.

Sprint Spectrum is a partnership of Sprint, Tele-Communications Inc, Cox Communications Inc and Comcast Corp. It plans to launch its national digital personal communications service in 15 to 20 markets by the end of 1996.
